sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong quarter with revenue up 8% YoY and EPS up 29% YoY, but forward guidance is largely reaffirmed rather than raised. Full-year 2025 expense guidance was raised to '~$84 billion, at the high end of the previous range,' and NII ex-Markets guidance was held at 'up ~4%'. The CEO's language is confident ('another very good quarter'), but the lack of a formal revenue or earnings guidance raise and the explicit expense guidance increase cap the score at mildly positive. The improvement is organic, not attributed to FX or one-time items.

summary.revenue: Total revenues, net of interest expense of $21,668 million for 2Q25, up 8% from $20,032 million in 2Q24.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $1.96 for 2Q25, up 29% from $1.52 in 2Q24.
summary.guidance: Full year 2025 expenses guided to '~$84 billion, at the high end of the previous range'. NII ex-Markets guided to 'up ~4%'. Targeting 10-11% RoTCE in 2026.
summary.margin: Efficiency ratio of 62.7% for 2Q25, improved 340 bps from 66.1% in 2Q24. Net interest margin (NIM) of 2.51% for 2Q25, up 10 bps from 2.41% in 2Q24.
key_risks: Higher cost of credit: 'Cost of credit of $2.9 billion increased 16%, driven by a higher net build in the allowance for credit losses (ACL) related to deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook'
Higher expenses: 'Full year 2025 expenses guided to ~$84 billion, at the high end of the previous range'
Increase in non-accrual loans: 'Total non-accrual loans increased 49% from the prior-year period to $3.4 billion'
Divestiture-related losses: '2Q25 includes (i) an approximately $186 million loss recorded in revenue... related to the announced sale of the Poland consumer banking business'
Transfer risk in Russia: 'The net ACL build was primarily related to transfer risk associated with client activity in Russia'
key_opportunities: Revenue growth across all five businesses: 'driven by growth in each of Citi’s five interconnected businesses'
Market share gains in Services: 'TTS: #1 Rank... gained ~40 bps of market share YoY'
Strong performance in Markets: 'Markets had its best second quarter performance since 2020 with a record second quarter for Equities'
Wealth revenue growth: 'Wealth revenues were up 20% with solid growth across all three lines of business'
Capital return to shareholders: 'Returned ~$3.1 billion to common shareholders through share repurchases and dividends in 2Q25'
Transformation and technology progress: 'Made significant progress on the Transformation and are now at or mostly at Citi’s target state for many programs'

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Jane Fraser stated 'We reported another very good quarter and continue to demonstrate that our strong results are sustainable through different environments.'
